 JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR                      §
 ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC                   §
 AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES                  §
                                                           BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
 CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR                      §
 CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND                 §
 NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY                   §
 EAST SWITCH TO THE BIG HILL                     §
                                                                         OF
 SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION                  §
 LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,                   §
 CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                      §
 LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH,                        §
                                                          ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
 MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA,                 §
 SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND                      §
 WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                             §

                            NEWMAN GROUP’S REPLY BRIEF

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

       The intervenors, Newman Surface Properties, LP (NSP; Party Nos. 565 and 566) and

Cherokee Camp, LLC (Cherokee Camp; Party No. 478) (collectively the Newman Group; Party

No. 565), timely file this their Reply Brief in the above-referenced cause arguing that the ALJs and

the Commission select Route 894, or in the alternative, any route that does not include the south-

ern routes in the study area, specifically Links J31, J32, J33, J6, K41, K42, M31, M32, and M33.

I.     INTRODUCTION

       1.      Route 894 is the best route for the Applicants’ 765-kV electric transmission line

after balancing all the record evidence with the statutory and regulatory routing criteria in this

case. The Newman Group urges the ALJs and the Commission to select Route 894. And in sup-

port, the Newman Group joins with its southern route neighbors: (a) the Colorado River Alliance;

(b) the Yates Keith Alliance; (c) the J6, K41, and J33 Landowner Group: and (d) the M31, M32,

and M33 Opposition Landowners opposing Routes 295/296, 572, and CCG.

       2.      Before replying further, however, the Newman Group must correct a mistake in
                 Newman Group’s Reply Brief in SOAH Dkt. No. 473-26-16349; PUC Dkt. No. 59475


Appendix B to the Applicants’ Initial Brief. There, the Applicants’ inadvertently omitted the New-

man Group, both individually and in their aligned party name, from their Initial Brief’s Appendix

B.1 The undersigned lead counsel attended in person and participated every day of the hearing on

the merits on the Newman Group’s behalf.2

II.       ROUTE 894 WINS OVER ROUTES 295/296, 572, AND CCG AFTER
          BALANCING ALL ROUTING CRITERIA WITH THE RECORD EVIDENCE

          3.        After balancing all routing criteria with the record evidence, Route 894 performs

the best in this case. Former PUC Chairman Barry Smitherman described the balancing test in his

direct testimony:

               Both the statute [PURA] and the rule provide for a subjective balancing of
               factors. In other words, no single or multiple factors automatically take prec-
               edence over another. ... However, once specific facts are established in the
               record, it may be shown that there are specific environmental concerns with
               a particular route or segment that need to be weighted heavily.3

Smitherman further testified “[i]t would be inappropriate to consider any factor or subset of factors

in isolation.”4 Oncor’s routing expert, Brenda Perkins, testified that “all of the other 36 factors in

the environmental table were – including cost and constructability were factored in in that deci-

sion.”5 When asked in her experience if “length, cost, and habitable structures tend to be viewed

by the [C]ommissioners as important factors,” Perkins then answered “[a]bsolutely.”6 For a more

detailed rebuttal of Routes 295/296, 572, and CCG, the Newman Group refers the ALJs and the

Commission to the Initial Briefs filed by the Colorado River Alliance, the Yates Keith Alliance,


1 See Oncor & LCRA – TSC Initial Br. App. B.

2 See Tr. Vol. 3 at 81:23 – 82:10. (J. Ross identifying his clients, including the Newman Group with their Party numbers

assigned by the ALJs in SOAH Order No. 31).
3 See Carpenter Ex. 3 at 9:3 – 8 (emphasis added).

4 See id. at 11:10 – 11.

5 See Tr. Vol. 2 at 94:19 – 21. (The Applicants’ selection of Route 894 as the “best meets” route).

6 See id. at 94:23 – 95:1.




                                                      Page 2 of 6
                  Newman Group’s Reply Brief in SOAH Dkt. No. 473-26-16349; PUC Dkt. No. 59475


the J6, K41, and J33 Landowner Group, and the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners.

The Newman Group points to specific facts below that weigh heavily in the record tipping the

balance of all the routing factors in favor of Route 894 and against Routes 295/296, 572, and

CCG.

          A.        The Florence ISD Elementary School in Link F34 Along with Other
                    Routing Factors Dooms Routes 295/296

          4.        The presence of Florence ISD’s new elementary school less than 400 feet from Link

F34 – a link in Routes 295 and 296 – coupled with the other routing criteria overwhelmingly

outweighs selecting Routes 295 or 296. Save the Lampasas’s reliance on PUC Dkt. No. 58276 is

misplaced.7 There, the Commission selected a route that was shorter, less expensive, and had fewer

habitable structures for a double-circuit 138-kV transmission line.8 In contrast and when compared

with Route 894, Routes 295 and 296 are a little longer (0.71 and 0.61 miles), more expensive ($1.975

and $3.644 million), and have more habitable structures within 500 feet of the routes’ centerline (19

and 20) for this 765-kV transmission line.9 The Newman Group asserts the Florence ISD elemen-

tary school is the heavy, determinative fact that tips the balancing of the routing criteria requiring

the ALJs and Commission to reject Routes 295 and 296 and select Route 894.

          B.        Route 572 Proponents Undervalue the Importance of Avoiding Paral-
                    leling the San Saba and Colorado Rivers

          5.        The Route 572 proponents overlook and undervalue the importance of minimizing

crossing or paralleling the San Saba and Colorado Rivers. Former PUC Commissioner McAdams,

testifying on behalf of the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners, determined that Route



7 See Save the Lampasas Initial Br. at 33.

8 See Application of the City of San Antonio, Acting by and Through the City Public Service Board (CPS Energy), to Amend its Certificate

of Convenience and Necessity for the Omicron 138-KV Transmission Line in Bexar County, Docket No. 58276, Order (Dkt. No.
58276) (Mar. 12, 2026) at 1.
9 See Oncor & LCRA – TSC Ex. 5 at 82 (Routes 295 & 296) & 101 (Route 894).




                                                             Page 3 of 6
                 Newman Group’s Reply Brief in SOAH Dkt. No. 473-26-16349; PUC Dkt. No. 59475


572 impacts much more of the San Saba and Colorado Rivers than Route 894.10 Throughout the

hearing on the merits, intervenors testified and asked questions about flooding on the San Saba

River.11 Selecting Route 894 reduces the potential impacts of river flooding to the grid unlike

Route 572. And when factoring in the other metrics, such as route length, cost, and habitable

structures, Route 572 (2.52 miles longer, $8.33 million more, and 22 more habitable structures)

performs worse than Route 894.12 As such, the Newman Group asks the ALJs and Commission to

reject Route 572.

         C.        Route CCG Cannot Overcome Its Deficiencies to Route 894

         6.        The Route CCG proponents cannot overcome their proposed RFI route’s major

and collective deficiencies when compared to Route 894. Oncor’s routing expert, Perkins, testified

on the first day of the hearing on the merits, “length, cost, and habitable structures tend to be

viewed by the [C]ommissioners as important factors.”13 Route CCG is 9.02 miles longer, $73.688

million costlier, and has 20 more habitable structures than Route 894.14 Moreover, Route CCG

has or crosses more:

         •    streams (346 v. 291);
         •    length across lakes or ponds (0.55 v. 0.4);
         •    recorded cultural resources within 1000 feet of the route (18 v. 12);
         •    length of route across areas of high archeological/historical site potential (62.79 v.
              54.34);
         •    private airstrips within 10,000 feet of the route (3 v. 2);
         •    FAA-registered airports (5 v. 3);


10 See M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners Ex. 9 at 13:13 – 22 (Routes 572 and CCG parallel or cross about

11.59 and 8.89 more miles of the San Saba and Colorado Rivers than Route 894 at 5.14 miles).
11 See, e.g., Tr. Vol. 4 at 182:20 – 25 (G. Nobles cross of J. Poole).

12 See Oncor & LCRA – TSC Ex. 5 at 95 (Route 572) & 101 (Route 894).

13 See Tr. Vol. 2 at 94:23 – 95:1.

14 See Cherokee Creek Ptnrs. Ex. 20 at 7 – 8; Oncor & LCRA – TSC Ex. 5 at 101 (Route 894).




                                                         Page 4 of 6
                    Newman Group’s Reply Brief in SOAH Dkt. No. 473-26-16349; PUC Dkt. No. 59475


             •    FM, microwave, & other electronic installations within 2000 feet (9 v. 5); and
             •    Farm to market, county roads & other street crossings (71 v. 47) than Route 894.15

Applying former Chairman Smitherman’s subjective balancing test, the abundance of routing cri-

teria tip heavily in favor of Route 894 over CCG. As such, the Newman Group asks the ALJs and

the Commission to reject Route CCG.

III.         OTHER ROUTES OF INTEREST

             7.      Without comparing the merits of their routing characteristics, the Newman Group

does not oppose Routes 392, 410, 487, 891, or 894 Western Mod 1. None of them include Links

J6 or K41, which cross the Newman Group’s ranches.

IV.          CONCLUSION

             8.      The Newman Group asks the ALJs and the Commission to select Route 894. It best

balances the routing criteria over every competing route, and especially Routes 295/296, 572, and

CCG. The Newman Group further asks for all other relief it is justly entitled to.
